subject: Rebrandable runtime license & SSO integration for NimblyTech
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@nimblytech.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: rebrandable model runtime & SSO options

Hi Camila,

Hope you’re well — I’m Jordan, Head of Product at NimblyTech. We’re evaluating vendors for an embeddable LLM runtime that our enterprise customers can rebrand inside their admin consoles. High-level asks: rebrandable runtime (logo/skin), support for our SSO (SAML + OIDC), and clear licensing for embedding the runtime inside customer-facing SaaS offerings.

Key drivers: we need predictable per-seat costs, telemetry that doesn’t include customer PII, and an option for us to white-label the UI while Redwood handles inference and model updates.

Would Redwood support a rebrandable runtime and what licensing structure do you typically offer for ISV integrations? Also, do you have an SSO integration guide we can review?

Thanks — if it helps, looping in our procurement alias contracts@nimblytech.com after we have a rough idea.

—Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Product, NimblyTech
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@nimblytech.com>
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: rebrandable model runtime & SSO options

Hi Jordan — great to meet you over email. Thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front: yes, we support co-branding/rebrandable UIs for partner integrations and we have a documented SSO integration path that covers both SAML and OIDC. For licensing, we offer a few patterns (per-seat, committed capacity + OEM addendum, and revenue-share bundles) depending on partner preference and volume.

I’ve attached a first-pass draft of a rebrandable license we usually start from for ISV partners (redwood_rebrand_license_draft_v1.pdf). To move forward efficiently I’d suggest a quick 30-min sync this week to align on: 1) desired license pattern, 2) telemetry/data boundaries, 3) SSO flow (IdP-initiated vs SP-initiated), and 4) rollout cadence for model updates.

Looping in Sergio (partnerships) to coordinate commercial approach. If you want legal involved early, we can add Laura.

Availability: I have Wed/Thu mornings PST open. What works for you?

Best,
Camila Reyes
Partner Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@nimblytech.com>, contracts@nimblytech.com
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: rebrandable model runtime & SSO options — draft + next steps

Jordan / Contracts team — attaching the draft license that outlines the OEM addendum, rebranding rights, and telemetry commitments. A few notes inline in the draft, and a short summary here:

- Proposed commercial structure: 12-month committed capacity + OEM addendum (annual true-up). We can also pilot a revenue-share model for channel-sold customers if that’s preferable.
- Rebranding scope: partner may change UI assets/branding; Redwood retains ownership of the runtime and model. Partners may apply their logo/brand to the partner-facing admin screens.
- Telemetry: we propose metric-only telemetry by default (latency, error rates, token counts) and an opt-in minimal logging path for debugging (PII redaction required).
- SSO: we support SAML 2.0 (IdP-initiated + SP-initiated) and OIDC; we’ll provide SP metadata and example Assertion Consumer Service endpoints.

Attachments: redwood_rebrand_license_draft_v1.pdf (contract draft), integration checklist (link in Drive).

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal review from your side (contracts@nimblytech.com)
2) Technical call to map SSO and auth flows (we can do a short architecture review)
3) Finalize commercial pattern (committed vs revenue share)

Sergio — can you take point on pricing scenarios and put together an example pricing table for Nimbly? Markus — please include any infra constraints for a rebrandable hosting model.

Thanks — Camila
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: contracts@nimblytech.com, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: rebrandable model runtime & SSO options — redlines and questions

Hi Jordan / Nimbly contracts team — I reviewed the draft and attached a redlined PDF with comments (redlined_license_v1.pdf). High-level items we need clarification on:

1) Data residency and audit scope — the draft currently allows telemetry aggregation in Redwood’s EU/US regions. If Nimbly requires strict per-customer residency, we’ll need to scope a Dedicated/Private deployment.
2) Ownership of derived outputs — we propose language that grants partners usage rights to outputs generated through their customers, with Redwood retaining rights to model improvements.
3) Indemnity and export controls — flagged a clause for export control carve-outs that Nimbly should confirm.

Also: we require confirmation that the partner will not surface raw model logs to customers. We can permit sanitized debug bundles under NDA.

Happy to hop on a legal + product sync to resolve.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@nimblytech.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, contracts@nimblytech.com
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@consultco.io>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: rebrandable model runtime & SSO options — redlines and next steps

Camila / Laura / Sergio — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. We reviewed internally; responses below: 

- Residency: Nimbly is comfortable starting with multi-region telemetry aggregation (US + EU) for the pilot customers. For enterprise customers with strict residency requirements we’ll evaluate Private deployment per customer.
- Derived outputs: Agreed to partner usage rights for outputs; we’ll accept Redwood’s suggested language on model improvement ownership.
- Logs: we will not surface raw model logs to end-customers; debug bundles only under NDA.

Next steps:
1) We’ll share a signed copy of the attached redlines from our contracts team by end of week.
2) Technical call: proposed Thurs 18 Jun 10:00 AM PST to map SSO flow (SAML IdP-initiated for our customers).
3) Commercial: please send the example pricing scenarios — Sergio, Camila — so we can lock on pilot terms.

Attached: nimbly_architecture_customer_flow.png (internal architecture snapshot). I’ve also uploaded an initial DocuSign packet here: https://www.docusign.com/Start/NIM-2026-042 — contracts will use that once legal confirms.

Appreciate the responsiveness — excited to get this moving.

—Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Product, NimblyTech
